newsitem.title: JAPAN: Discovery Channel begins 24-hour Japan broadcast.
newsitem.headline: Discovery Channel begins 24-hour Japan broadcast.

text.p: Discovery Japan Inc said on Friday it had launched this week a 24-hour non-fiction entertainment broadcasting network in Japan.

Discovery Channel, which is seen in 140 countries worldwide, will be fully subtitled in Japanese and available on the PerfecTV satellite channel and some regional cable networks, Discovery Japan said in a statement.
PerfecTV, a venture owned by a consortium of Japanese trading companies, began broadcasting last year.
The channel will feature documentaries on various subjects such as nature, history, culture, science and technology, Discovery Japan said.

The company is a joint venture with Singapore-based Discovery Asia Inc -- a unit of U.S. company Discovery Communications Inc, which runs the Discovery Channel worldwide -- and Tokyo-based Jupiter Programming Co Ltd.
Jupiter said the launch of the network will fuel growth in cable and satellite television services in Japan.
"The move marks a step forward in providing quality programming essential for a multi-channel era in the Japanese market," Jupiter Chairman Yasushige Nishimura said in the statement.
Jupiter is jointly operated by U.S.-based Telecommunications International Inc and Japanese trading house Sumitomo Corp.
The launch of the new channel is the latest in an intensifying battle between three fledgling satellite broadcasting services in Japan.

In June, Turner Broadcasting System Asia Pacific Inc, Itochu Corp and Time Warner Entertainment Japan Inc (TWEJ) said they would jointly launch in September the Cartoon Network Japan, the nation's first 24-hour cartoon channel.
